subject: Everspring Health — HIPAA evidence scope, BAA exceptions and timeline

Subject: RFP follow-up — HIPAA evidence & BAA scope

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our vendor risk review we've compiled a short evidence request and an outline of contract items we need to get aligned on before legal will greenlight a POC. High level:

- A completed HIPAA control matrix mapping (attestation + evidence)
- Dataflow diagram showing PHI ingress/egress + retention points
- Confirmation of encryption at rest and in transit (KMS/HSM details if available)
- Proposed BAA; we have a few non-standard exceptions we want to discuss (retention carve-outs, subprocessor notification SLA)

Can you confirm whether you can deliver the matrix and a dataflow PDF by EOD Friday? Also please include any standard BAA you typically sign so our counsel can do a first pass. If not, propose a timeline.

We may ask for SOC2/ISO excerpts later but this first pass is focused on HIPAA readiness.

Thanks — looking to move quickly.

Samantha Ortiz
Director, Vendor Risk
Everspring Health

+1 617-555-0132

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — HIPAA evidence & BAA scope

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can supply the HIPAA control mapping and a dataflow diagram by EOD Friday (2026-10-02) as requested. Attached: Redwood_HIPAA_Readiness_Matrix_v1.3.pdf and redwood-dataflow-everspring-2026.pdf — both are mapped to your template where possible.

Quick notes up front:
- Encryption: All customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256; we integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) for customer-managed keys in Private deployments. For hosted accounts we offer a Redwood-managed KMS option; details included in matrix.
- Retention: Default retention windows are configurable per-customer; standard hosted retention is 30 days for request logs and 180 days for user content unless contractually configured.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a subprocessors registry and a 30-day notification SLA for new subprocessors; we can discuss exceptions.

We will also drop a proposed BAA for your counsel to review — Markus (our contracts lead) will attach a draft by Monday with the redline for your team.

If you want a brief call to walk through the matrix before legal reviews, I'm available Fri 10/2 between 11–1 PT.

Thanks,

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Healthcare
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFP follow-up — HIPAA evidence & BAA scope

Team — quick internal thread before we send anything more to Everspring. A couple of clarifications I want to surface from the matrix:

1) KMS customer-managed keys: For Private deployments we can support external HSMs via KMIP, yes, but for hosted customers our KMS integration supports CMEK through cloud providers only (no bring-your-own-HSM in hosted). Need to be explicit to avoid surprises.

2) Retention exceptions: Procurement may ask for 7-year retention. We should flag a cost/technical impact if they require hosted logs/content beyond 365 days (storage and egress pricing).

3) Subprocessor notification: We currently do 30-day notification and a chance to review for large customers, but contractually we don't typically provide veto rights — propose we offer 90-day notice for enterprise deals as a concession, not veto.

Markus — can you prepare a short BAA addendum that explicitly notes the notification SLA and the retention carve-out language (we'll mark them as negotiable)? Also include the encryption options (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed) so counsel has implementation language.

I'll draft a short email to Samantha confirming delivery and proposed timing for the BAA draft.

— Stephanie
Sr. Account Executive, Healthcare Sales
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@everspringhealth.com>, legal@everspringhealth.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: BAA addendum — proposed language and redline summary

Hi Samantha / Everspring counsel —

Following Vivek's delivery of the matrix, please find attached a proposed BAA addendum (BAA-Addendum_PROPOSED_2026-10-05.docx) and a short redline summary. A few key points we addressed based on your initial note and our internal product constraints:

- Subprocessor Notification: We propose a 30-day notice for new subprocessors with an option to negotiate a 90-day notice for enterprise contracts. We are not able to accept vendor veto on subprocessors; instead we offer enhanced audit rights and an escalation path.
- Retention: We included language to support contractually extended retention windows. For hosted deployments, extended retention beyond 365 days will incur additional fees and may require a dedicated storage tier; we flagged the pricing impact in the addendum.
- Encryption & Key Management: Draft includes both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed key (CMEK) options. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, HSM/KMIP integrations are supported and show as mandatory where requested.
- Incident Notification: We commit to 72-hour initial notification for incidents involving PHI and standard remediation cooperation.

I've also attached supporting-evidence-index.csv which maps the matrix items to the evidence artifacts we can provide (reports, config screenshots, runbooks). If any of these items are insufficient, please let us know which specific artifacts your counsel requires.

Next steps: If the addendum is acceptable in principle, we can circulate a DocuSign envelope for signature and request a short call between legal teams to resolve the few open carve-outs (retention, notification SLA).

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal Operations
markus_klein@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
